title: Mnesis CanonicalFrame
description: One frame of embodied spatial-action data = one JSONL line. Open standard, Apache-2.0. Authority: SPEC.md / Parthenon 03 §3.2. Keep in lock-step with schema.py.

index.description: Global monotonic frame index across episodes.

frame_index.description: Frame index within episode (0-based, strictly increasing — cross-frame rule enforced by validate_frames).

t_hw_ns.description: Hardware ns (ARCore frame.timestamp) — join key pose<->video.

observation.state.description: 7-DoF state (ego_v1) or variable-length float[N] (robot_v2, N per registry joint_names).

observation.images.ego.description: File reference to the ego video frame ('' allowed). Required for ego_v1 profile.

action.description: Relative delta [tx,ty,tz, rx,ry,rz] (m, axis-angle rad) for ego_v1; variable-length for robot_v2.

spatial_anchor_pose_SE3.description: The ANCHOR's own pose in the world frame [tx,ty,tz, qx,qy,qz,qw] (optional). This — not head_pose_SE3 — is what identifies an anchor. Supply it when the capture surface can localise the anchor; conflicting definitions of the same spatial_anchor_id are then detected against it. Omit when unavailable: the anchor id is still carried, only the consistency check is skipped.

space_id.description: Shared physical-space identifier (C8, additive). All devices in the same physical space use the same value, enabling cross-device episode merge/alignment. Orthogonal to spatial_anchor_id (per-engine anchor namespace). Absent = space unknown.

source.device.description: Capture surface, e.g. phone, glasses, quest, pico, robot, sim (open set).

source.modality.description: Capture modality, e.g. ego_human, teleop, robot_replay, sim (open set).

profile.description: Frame profile (v0.2+). When absent, defaults to ego_v1 (backward-compatible).

embodiment_id.description: Reference to an embodiment registry entry (v0.2+). Optional.

observation.eef_pose.left.description: Left end-effector pose [tx,ty,tz, qx,qy,qz,qw] (robot_v2 profile, optional).

observation.eef_pose.right.description: Right end-effector pose [tx,ty,tz, qx,qy,qz,qw] (robot_v2 profile, optional).

action.gripper.description: Optional gripper channel (v0.4+, additive, all profiles). Normalized 0.0 (fully open) .. 1.0 (fully closed). Absent = source provides no gripper info (NOT 0.0). Physical stroke is described by the embodiment registry, not per-frame.

observation.gripper.description: Optional gripper observation closedness [0,1] (0.0=fully open, 1.0=fully closed). Additive, any profile; direction identical to action.gripper and C3 xr_bridge arms[].gripper. Single / main gripper.

observation.gripper.left.description: Optional left gripper observation closedness [0,1] (0.0=fully open, 1.0=fully closed). robot_v2 bimanual, additive.

observation.gripper.right.description: Optional right gripper observation closedness [0,1] (0.0=fully open, 1.0=fully closed). robot_v2 bimanual, additive.

observation.hand.left.description: [experimental] Left-hand joint POSITIONS, flattened [x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ...] in metres, length 3*K where K is the joint_count of the layout named by observation.hand.layout (skeletons/<id>.json). Variable-length by design: a fixed length would freeze one vendor's hand topology into the standard. A hand that is not tracked is OMITTED ENTIRELY — never a zero vector, never null — so 'no hand' stays distinguishable from 'hand at the origin'. Requires observation.hand.layout and observation.hand.frame.

observation.hand.right.description: [experimental] Right-hand joint POSITIONS. Same rules as observation.hand.left.

observation.hand.left.rot.description: [experimental] Optional left-hand joint ORIENTATIONS, flattened quaternions {x,y,z,w} (scalar last, right-handed — same order as head_pose_SE3), length 4*K for the same layout. Filled only by sources that natively provide per-joint orientation (OpenXR / WebXR hand tracking); MediaPipe-class sources omit it. Skeleton retargeting consumes this. Requires observation.hand.left.

observation.hand.right.rot.description: [experimental] Optional right-hand joint ORIENTATIONS. Same rules as observation.hand.left.rot.

observation.hand.layout.description: [experimental] Skeleton layout id declaring the joint count and per-index meaning of the hand keypoint vectors, e.g. 'mediapipe_hand_21' | 'webxr_hand_25' | 'openxr_hand_26'. Resolved against the skeleton registry (skeletons/<id>.json), the same mechanism by which embodiment_id declares the layout of observation.state. Required whenever a hand keypoint vector is present.

observation.hand.frame.description: [experimental] Reference frame of the hand keypoints — the machine-readable form of the '2.5D, not true 3D' caveat. 'world' = same world frame as head_pose_SE3. 'head_anchored' = metric and self-consistent WITHIN the hand, placed at the head/camera and rotated by the head pose, but the hand's absolute position relative to the world is NOT recovered (monocular world-landmark estimators land here). 'hand_local' = origin is the hand itself; no world placement claimed. Consumers needing world-localised hands MUST filter on frame == 'world' rather than on a source string. Required whenever a hand keypoint vector is present.

observation.hand.source.description: [experimental] Provenance label for the hand keypoints (open set), e.g. 'mediapipe_world+arcore_pose' for an on-device estimate or an offline-refinement tag. Optional, and provenance ONLY — geometric semantics live in observation.hand.frame, not here.

^x-[a-z][a-z0-9-_]*\\..description: Vendor extension namespace (x-<vendor>.<field>). Reserved for vendor-specific extensions. See extensions/registry.json and SPEC.md §Conventions.
